title: Drop gate scopes: completion findings fail the step like invariants; the scope provider, closure, the pending state and `gate-pending` are removed

ground.note: The abandoned first version (approved 2026-10-05, abandoned 2026-10-06), with its sidecar. Its context, surface and §9 Q1–Q5 are the ground for the decisions carried over here. It depended on gate-request, put `"input": "gate-request"` on the hello-world step, and left open how the format changes meet the history convention and the docs site.

Draft. Lands first. Its after-state is this spec's before-state: hello-world declares `scopes`, `planAuditor` and the diagnostics step, README §Extend phax says "Three hooks", and the announcement draft counts two providers. It defines kept history and the live tree, and checks its removal with a mechanical sweep. This spec reuses both definitions.

Draft. Lands after this spec and describes the gate as this spec leaves it: no `scopes` provider, closure, pending state, `pending` result or `gate-pending`, and no `stdin:` line in the attempt log. Nothing in it needs changing.

§Extend phax: "Four hooks" today (three after drop-orient). §Diagnostics gate steps: "A `completion` finding names the `scopes` it belongs to, and fails the step only once all of them are closed according to your scope provider; until then it is pending, shown to the agent as optional work." §Scope provider: the `{phase, phases}` request and the `{"closed": [...]}` answer. §Persisted formats: the `gate-pending` row, and the promise that each `$schema` URL "stays up for good".

Once per attempt and before any step, the closure is resolved: `all` on the terminal phase, otherwise a query to the scope provider when the profile has a diagnostics step, or `unavailable` when no provider is configured. The query is logged as `$ <cmd>`, `stdin: <json>` and the answer. Also here: `scheduleDiagnostics`, the `missing-provider` configuration error, `result: "pending"`, `writePendingDoc` and `pendingPathFor`, and `DIAGNOSTICS_EXPECTED_SHAPE`, which names `"scopes"?`. The diagnostics file holds the whole decoded document.

`ScopeClosure` is all | closed | unavailable. An invariant always fails. A completion fails when every scope it names is closed and is pending otherwise. With `unavailable`, any completion yields `missing-provider`.

A failing finding renders as `- <rule> at <file:line> — <message>` plus `  repair guide: …`, with no class shown. `## Pending (optional — not required to pass this gate)` is appended to both the diagnostics prompt and the log-failure prompt whenever the attempt holds pending findings.

A completion is `{class: "completion", scopes: NonEmptyArray, rule, location, message, repair}`. An invariant is the same without `scopes`. The file shape is `$schema` followed by the stdout document.
`{closed: [...], steps: [{command, pending: [{diagnostic, openScopes}]}]}` under a `gate-pending` `$schema`.
A step result is `"pass" | "fail" | "pending"`. Only `pass` verifies a surface.

The scope provider's answer `{closed: [...]}`. The request type `ScopesRequest` and `makeScopesRequest` live in src/domain/plan/projection.ts, beside `projectPhases` and `makePlanAuditRequest`, which the plan auditor keeps using. The query itself runs through src/app/scopes.ts.

`ScopesConfigSchema {command}` sits in the project schema and the user overlay, and its description names closure and pending. `GATE_OUTPUT_DESCRIPTION` names `"scopes"?` and ends with the pending rule. Both schemas reject excess properties.
`scopes.command` comes from phax.local.json, then ~/.phax/config.json, then phax.json. src/app/loadConfig.ts passes it through.

Passes `scopesProvider` and `makeScopesRequest(...)` to the gate. On a green gate with pending findings it prints `[phax] phase "<id>" gate: green — N completion diagnostic(s) pending (scopes still open: …)`. `PendingStep` (src/domain/errors.ts) flows through `GatePassed`/`GateFailed` (src/domain/events.ts), src/app/eventAdapter.ts and src/app/fixLoop.ts. `ScopesProviderError` is in src/domain/errors.ts.

phax reads `gate-attribution.json` for verified surfaces: a `$schema` document with its current decoder only, a document without one with the frozen pre-schema module. A document that fails to decode counts as no verified surface. phax never reads `.diagnostics.json` or `.pending.json`.

`phax.json` declares `scopes` (`node ./scopes.mjs`), `planAuditor` and the diagnostics step `node ./audit.mjs`. `audit.mjs` ignores stdin and emits only invariants (`HW_NO_IO`), so the example never produces a completion. tests/integration/exampleProviders.test.ts runs `scopes.mjs`.

`gate-attribution`, `gate-diagnostics` and `gate-pending` each have a frozen pre-schema module, `releases: []`, and a current shape that is phax's own file schema. Each `toLatest*` drops `$schema` and keeps every other fact.

A shape change is recorded as `next.schema.json`, which the release cut renames. A released snapshot is never rewritten or removed. A released snapshot that is no longer current needs a frozen decoder in the format's `releases` ("freeze it as src/schemas/history/<id>/<release>.ts").

Checks the generated index (`CURRENT_SHAPES`), the history lock against every module under src/schemas/history/ in both directions (a lock entry for a missing module is a finding, as is a module with no entry), and the snapshots.
Pins 15 pre-schema modules, among them gate-attribution, gate-diagnostics and gate-pending. The gate-diagnostics module holds `scopes` and the gate-attribution module holds `"pending"`.

PACKAGE_VERSION 0.19.0, FIRST_SUPPORTED_RELEASE 0.17.0. The current shape of gate-attribution, gate-diagnostics and gate-pending is `0.17.0`. This is the first change to a gate format since `$schema`.
Promises that every file written from phax 0.17.0 on stays readable.

For every release in packages/schemas/releases.json (0.17.0, 0.18.0, 0.19.0) and every id in FORMAT_IDS, serves the latest released snapshot at /schemas/<id>/<release>.json and lists the path in /schemas/index.json. `pre-schema` and `next` are never served.

Refuses any build that does not serve a path the live https://docs.phax.run/schemas/index.json lists. Removing `gate-pending` from FORMAT_IDS and its snapshots would drop /schemas/gate-pending/0.17.0.json, 0.18.0.json and 0.19.0.json, so the guard would refuse.

The guard runs before any upload in the release and docs-deploy workflows, and a refusal stages nothing. The release cut renames `next` snapshots and appends the release to the ledger. docs.phax.run has been live since v0.18.0 (NEXT_STEPS).

Approved, not built. It quotes the diagnostics shape with `scopes?` (ground), the attribution result as pass|fail|pending (ground and §5), and `scopes` in §1, in its projection and README ground lines, and in two config examples. Its non-goals list "deriving oracles from `scopes`". Its `oracles` key "mirrors `scopes` and `planAuditor`" and appears in the user overlay "like `scopes`".

The gates section (lines ~88–95) describes completion findings as pending work until the phase that owns them lands. The providers list (after drop-orient: two providers) has a `scopes` bullet, and the closing line says "offered at … points".
coverage-provider.md lists `scopes` among the existing providers. change-gates-from-the-harness.md mentions "`scopes` closure".
Has no scope, closure or pending-finding text. Its only occurrences of "pending" concern pending phases and pending records, which are unrelated.

§Before steme's audit (reordered 2026-10-06): drop-orient, then drop-gate-scopes, then gate-request and the brief. It records that nobody configures `scopes` or reads the diagnostics output, and has an item to sweep the `oracle-phases` wording. §Road to 1.0.0: the CLI and config contract freeze and the persisted-format stability promise.

context:
This spec starts from the gate as `drop-orient` leaves it: there is no `orient` hook, and README §Extend phax lists three hooks (Diagnostics gate steps, Scope provider, Plan auditor).

A gate step with `"output": "diagnostics"` prints `{ "diagnostics": [...] }`. Each finding is either an `invariant` (something forbidden is present) or a `completion` (something required is missing), and carries `rule`, `location: {file, line?}`, `message` and `repair`. A completion must also carry `scopes`, a non-empty list of names. An empty list with exit 0 passes. A missing or undecodable document, or an empty list with a non-zero exit, is a provider error that fails the step.

Once per gate attempt, before any step runs, phax resolves scope closure. On the terminal phase every scope is closed. On any other phase whose profile has a diagnostics step, phax runs the configured `scopes` command with `{phase, phases}` on stdin, writes `$ <cmd>`, `stdin: <json>` and the answer to the attempt log, and reads `{"closed": [...]}`. If the provider fails, the gate fails. If no provider is configured, any completion finding fails the step as a configuration error (`missing-provider`). An invariant fails the step, and so does a completion whose scopes are all closed. A completion with a scope still open is pending.

When a step returns only pending findings, `gate-attribution.json` records it as `pending`, which verifies no surface. Pending findings are written to `checks-attempt-NN.pending.json` (format `gate-pending`) and listed in the attempt's fix prompts under `## Pending (optional — not required to pass this gate)`. A green gate announces them as `N completion diagnostic(s) pending (scopes still open: …)`.

`scopes: {command}` is a key of `phax.json`, `phax.local.json` and `~/.phax/config.json`, and the nearest layer wins. `phax schema upgrade` regenerates `phax.schema.json` and `phax.user.schema.json`, whose gate-step `output` description ends with the pending rule. It never touches `phax.json`.

Nobody configures `scopes`, ships a scope provider or reads the diagnostics output: phax, steme-lab, phax-cockpit and louloupapers were checked on 2026-10-05. The only scope provider is phax's own `examples/hello-world/scopes.mjs`, and the example's `audit.mjs` emits only invariants. So no completion finding, `.pending.json` or `pending` result has ever been written outside phax's tests. The first real diagnostics provider will be steme's audit (`steme audit`, roadmap-1.0 item 0.13, not built yet), which reports only what is due and never emits a scope.

Persisted files carry the `$schema` URL `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/<format>/<release>.json`. `@lbdremy/phax-schemas` 0.19.0 reads `gate-diagnostics`, `gate-attribution` and `gate-pending`. Each has a frozen pre-schema module under `src/schemas/history/`, pinned by `packages/schemas/history.lock.json`, and each still has `0.17.0` as its current shape. The package's history convention works like this: a changed shape is recorded as `next.schema.json` and renamed by the release cut; a released snapshot is never removed; and a released snapshot that is no longer current needs a frozen decoder `src/schemas/history/<id>/<release>.ts` of its own.

docs.phax.run has been live since v0.18.0. For every release in the ledger (0.17.0 through 0.19.0) and every format, it serves the latest released snapshot at `/schemas/<id>/<release>.json` and lists that path in `/schemas/index.json`. Its deploy guard refuses any build that would stop serving a listed path, and README §Persisted formats promises that each URL "stays up for good".

The author's order (NEXT_STEPS §Before steme's audit, 2026-10-06) is drop-orient, then this spec, then gate-request and the brief. The first version of this spec, approved on 2026-10-05, depended on gate-request and carried compatibility niceties. It was abandoned on 2026-10-06.
problem:
phax schedules completion findings itself, so the question "is this finding due yet?" is split across two commands and two formats. The diagnostics step says what is wrong. A second provider, queried before the gate with its own request and answer shapes, says which scopes are closed. phax joins the two answers and keeps state it cannot judge: closure, pending findings, a `pending` step result that is neither pass nor fail, and a `gate-pending` record.

A provider that wants to say "not due yet" has to use phax's vocabulary. It must invent scope names, tag every completion with them, and ship a second command that recomputes closure from the plan. steme's audit, the first real provider, would have to build exactly that and later throw it away.

The agent pays too: its fix prompt mixes required work with "optional" work. And all of this is about to freeze with the 1.0 CLI and config contract (NEXT_STEPS §Road to 1.0.0). A key, a format and a step result that are still here at the freeze would have to be carried, or broken, after it. Nobody uses any of it, so removing it costs nothing now, and the cost only grows later.

productGoal.statement:
The diagnostics provider decides what is due and reports only that. phax runs the diagnostics step and reads its verdict, and does nothing more. A completion finding fails the step exactly as an invariant does. Both classes stay in the document, where they say which kind of failure it is: something required is missing, or something forbidden is present.

The `scopes` provider, closure resolution, the pending state, the `missing-provider` failure, the `pending` step result and the `gate-pending` record are removed. Nothing replaces them, and nothing eases their removal. `gate-diagnostics` and `gate-attribution` get next shapes, and `gate-pending` leaves the schemas package. The README, the example, the generated config schemas and the announcement draft stop describing any of it. Scope machinery survives only where history is kept on purpose. Everything else about the gate stays as it is.
productGoal.guidingRule: Every finding a diagnostics step reports is due: phax fails the step on it and keeps no schedule of its own.

terminology.definition: One entry of a diagnostics document's `diagnostics` array: `{rule, class, location: {file, line?}, message, repair}`.
A finding with `class: "completion"`: something the change requires is missing.
A finding with `class: "invariant"`: something the change forbids is present.
The command of a gate step that declares `"output": "diagnostics"`, such as hello-world's `audit.mjs` or, later, `steme audit`.
Ready to be judged now. After this spec, only the diagnostics provider decides what is due, from what it can read itself: git and the worktree. phax treats every reported finding as due.

What this spec removes: the `scopes` config key and its provider contract, closure resolution and its query, pending findings, the `pending` step result, `.pending.json` and the `gate-pending` format, the fix prompt's pending section, the green-gate pending line and the `missing-provider` failure. The term is used only to say what goes.
A format's changed shape. It is recorded as `packages/schemas/snapshots/<id>/next.schema.json` and published under the release that ships it, when the release cut renames the snapshot.

The modules under `src/schemas/history/` that `packages/schemas/history.lock.json` pins, and the released snapshots under `packages/schemas/snapshots/`. The package's history convention keeps them byte for byte.
A JSON Schema that docs.phax.run serves at `/schemas/<id>/<release>.json` and lists in `/schemas/index.json`. The deploy guard protects every listed path.

As drop-orient defines it: `docs/specs/` and `docs/plans/` (archived and live, with sidecars and approval records), `docs/briefs/`, `docs/spikes/` and `NEXT_STEPS.md`, plus the untracked git history, records on `phax/records/v1` and earlier phase folders. For this spec it also includes the frozen history of `gate-diagnostics` and `gate-attribution` and the served `gate-pending` schemas (§9 q-served).

Every tracked file that is not kept history: code, tests, scripts, packages, generated contract files, the README, `docs/` outside the kept paths (`docs/ideas/` included), examples and the shipped skills.

requirements.title: Any finding fails the step
requirements.statement: The system shall fail a diagnostics step whose document holds at least one finding, of either class, whatever the step's exit code.

requirements.title: One rule on every phase
requirements.statement: The system shall judge a diagnostics step's findings by the same rule on the terminal phase and on every other phase, taking nothing from the plan, the phase's position or git into the verdict.

requirements.title: The other verdict rules stay
requirements.statement: The system shall keep every other verdict rule of a diagnostics step as it is today: an empty list with exit 0 passes, and a missing or undecodable document, or an empty list with a non-zero exit, is a provider error that fails the step with the raw log.

requirements.title: The rest of the gate stays
requirements.statement: The system shall keep gate steps, their profile order, `surface`, `firing`, `output`, the stop at the first failing step, the fix loop and the attribution of every step that ran exactly as they are today.

requirements.title: Only the selected steps run
requirements.statement: WHEN a gate attempt runs THE system SHALL start no process other than the profile's selected steps and SHALL write to the attempt log only those steps' entries.

requirements.title: Attribution is pass or fail
requirements.statement: The system shall record every step that ran in `gate-attribution.json`, in the next `gate-attribution` shape, with a `result` of `"pass"` or `"fail"`.

requirements.title: The diagnostics file is the next shape
requirements.statement: WHEN a diagnostics step fails on its findings THE system SHALL save its document as `checks-attempt-NN.diagnostics.json` in the next `gate-diagnostics` shape.

requirements.title: No pending file
requirements.statement: The system shall write no `checks-attempt-NN.pending.json` file.

requirements.title: The provider error states the next shape
requirements.statement: IF a diagnostics step's document is missing or undecodable THEN the system SHALL state the expected document as `{"diagnostics": [{"rule", "class": "invariant"|"completion", "location": {"file", "line"?}, "message", "repair"}]}` in the provider error it logs and reports.

requirements.title: The fix prompt lists both classes alike
requirements.statement: WHEN a fix prompt lists a failing step's findings THE system SHALL list every finding in the provider's order, both classes alike, as it renders failing findings today, with no class tag and no legend.

requirements.title: No pending section
requirements.statement: The system shall build every fix prompt with no pending or optional-work section.

requirements.title: A green gate announces nothing pending
requirements.statement: WHEN a phase's gate passes THE system SHALL print the output it prints today for a passing gate with no findings, with no line counting pending findings.

requirements.title: No scope provider in the configuration contract
requirements.statement: The configuration contract of `phax.json`, `phax.local.json` and `~/.phax/config.json` shall have no scope provider key, and shall keep every other key and its layer precedence as they are today.

requirements.title: The local schemas follow the contract
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax schema upgrade` runs THE system SHALL write a `phax.schema.json` and a `phax.user.schema.json` whose top-level properties are exactly those of the configuration contract and whose gate-step `output` description names no scope, closure or pending finding, and SHALL leave `phax.json` unchanged.

requirements.title: `gate-diagnostics` next shape
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall publish as the `gate-diagnostics` next shape a document in which an invariant finding and a completion finding carry exactly the same fields: `rule`, `class`, `location: {file, line?}`, `message` and `repair`.

requirements.title: `gate-attribution` next shape
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall publish as the `gate-attribution` next shape a step `result` of exactly `pass` or `fail`.

requirements.title: `gate-pending` leaves the package
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall have no `gate-pending` format (no format id, parser, upgrade function, type, current or frozen shape, snapshot or JSON Schema), and README §Persisted formats shall have no `gate-pending` row.

requirements.title: The gate formats' history is kept as the convention requires
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall keep the frozen pre-schema modules and every released snapshot of `gate-diagnostics` and `gate-attribution` byte for byte, and shall read each of these formats' `0.17.0` shape through a frozen module of its own.

requirements.title: The history lock changes by three entries
requirements.statement: `packages/schemas/history.lock.json` shall differ from today's by exactly three entries: `src/schemas/history/gate-pending/pre-schema.ts` removed, and `src/schemas/history/gate-diagnostics/0.17.0.ts` and `src/schemas/history/gate-attribution/0.17.0.ts` added.

requirements.title: Served `gate-pending` URLs stay up
requirements.statement: The docs site shall keep serving byte for byte, and keep listing in `/schemas/index.json`, every `gate-pending` schema URL that docs.phax.run serves before this change, and shall serve no `gate-pending` URL for any later release.

requirements.title: The example has no scope provider
requirements.statement: The hello-world example shall declare no scope provider, ship no scope provider script, and keep its diagnostics step and `audit.mjs` as they are.

requirements.title: The docs describe no scope machinery
requirements.statement: The README, `phax --usage`, `phax.usage.kdl`, `docs/cli/reference.md`, the generated config schemas, `docs/blog/announcing-phax-1.0.md`, `docs/ideas/` and `examples/hello-world/` shall describe no scope provider, scope closure or pending finding, and README §Diagnostics gate steps shall state that an invariant finding and a completion finding both fail the step.

requirements.title: Counts match what is listed
requirements.statement: README §Extend phax shall state a hook count equal to the number of hook subsections it lists, and the 1.0 announcement draft shall state a provider count equal to the number of providers it lists.

requirements.title: The live tree is swept
requirements.statement: The live tree shall contain none of the scope machinery's identifiers, file names, config key or section names.

How the removals are split into phases. Suggested: gate code and tests first, then config and the generated schemas, then the schemas package and site, then docs, the example and the sweep, keeping each phase green under `pnpm check:full` (knip included).
constraints: Lands after `drop-orient` and before `gate-request` and the brief. Its surface starts from drop-orient's after-state: hello-world with `scopes`, `planAuditor` and the diagnostics step, README "Three hooks", and two providers in the announcement draft.
phax gains no notion of what is due. Nothing computed from the plan, the phase's position or git enters the verdict.

No requirement, criterion, test or doc names a leftover `scopes` key in a config layer or on a finding. Nothing restates the ordinary unknown-key refusal (exit 2) or the ordinary tolerance of extra keys on decode.
No shims and no compatibility code. Earlier-release gate files are read only through the frozen decoders the history convention requires.
This spec removes CLI and config surface on purpose before the 1.0 freeze: one config key, one provider contract, one step result, one phase-folder file and one persisted format. Nothing is added.
`gate-request` (Draft, docs/specs/2610060951-gate-request.md) already describes the gate as this spec leaves it, so its wording needs no change.

`oracle-phases` (Approved, not built) is not changed here. Wording its own revision must sweep: §1's bullet "`scopes` returns which completion scopes are closed…"; the ground lines on src/app/gates.ts ("A scopes-provider failure fails the gate"), src/schemas/gateDiagnostics.ts (`scopes?` in the shape), src/schemas/gateAttribution.ts (`pass|fail|pending`), src/schemas/phaxConfig.ts (the provider blocks list), the plan projection "sent to `scopes` and `planAuditor`" and README §Scope provider; §5's "its pass, fail or pending result" for the oracle step; the two config examples declaring `scopes`; the non-goal "deriving oracles from `scopes`"; and the `oracles` key notes "mirroring `scopes` and `planAuditor`" and "like `scopes`". After this spec those notes read as mirroring `planAuditor` alone, and its plan reads the diagnostics shape at build time, with no `scopes`.
NEXT_STEPS stays the author's queue: the `drop-gate-scopes` and `oracle-phases` wording items are ticked under the file's own rule.

docsPage.reader: The author of a diagnostics provider, such as steme's audit, who needs to know how phax judges findings now: both classes fail, and the provider alone decides what is due.
docsPage.example: Declare `{ "command": "node ./audit.mjs", "surface": "structural", "firing": "every-phase", "output": "diagnostics" }` in a gate profile. In audit.mjs, report an invariant whenever something forbidden is present. Report a completion such as `{ "rule": "wire-invoice-cli", "class": "completion", "location": { "file": "src/cli/index.ts" }, "message": "the invoice command is not registered", "repair": "register it" }` only once it is due, judged from what the provider can read itself (for example, once `src/cli/index.ts` exists in the worktree). Every reported finding fails the step, and the fix prompt lists it.
